investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a ready state, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent and every contract assertion is unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent feature has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. Every new remote-agent pod is rejected as Unschedulable before it can start, which means the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returns an agent or VM identity. The failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment; no evidence of a broader platform outage or user-traffic incident is present in the supplied packet.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod is unscheduled

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:179-187: remote-agent-create is marked required=true with degradedAfterFailures=1, so a single failure triggers a degraded signal for the remote-agents feature
possibleCauses: Primary: The kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable resource on the 2 eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing running remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero capacity for new pods. Preemption is explicitly reported as not helpful, meaning no lower-priority victims exist to evict.

Secondary: A prior eval run or production workload created remote-agent pods that were not cleaned up, holding the kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new scheduling. The eval runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1883), but if a previous run crashed before cleanup, leaked pods could be holding capacity.

Tertiary: The 4 remaining nodes do not carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource label or do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, meaning the schedulable node pool for remote agents is structurally limited to 2 nodes and any saturation of those nodes causes a total scheduling blackout for this feature.

Lower confidence: A cluster-level change (node drain, node failure, or resource quota reduction) may have reduced the effective kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity below what is needed to run concurrent eval probes. No infrastructure change evidence is present in the supplied packet to confirm this.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pods VM Capacity Exhausted on Production Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes cannot schedule the required kata.peerpods.io/vm pod because 2 nodes report insufficient kata peer-pod VM capacity and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never schedules, the eval runner's createAgent call never returns a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is ever written and the expected-output contract is fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler cannot place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource report that resource as exhausted (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the two eligible nodes and the four mismatched nodes are structurally ineligible. The pod remains Unschedulable for ~147 seconds until the eval times out, preventing agent creation entirely. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity or configuration failure localized to the remote-agent pod scheduling path in the production Kubernetes cluster; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

SECONDARY — node affinity or node selector misconfiguration on the remote agent pod spec: the 4 remaining nodes are structurally excluded by the pod's affinity/selector rules, meaning only 2 nodes are even candidates and both are at capacity. A misconfigured selector could be artificially narrowing the eligible node pool.

TERTIARY — cluster under-provisioning: the production cluster has only 6 nodes total, with only 2 carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource. If concurrent eval runs or production workloads consumed all available VM slots simultaneously, transient exhaustion would produce this exact error.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a ready state, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent and every contract assertion is unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent feature has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. Every new remote-agent pod is rejected as Unschedulable before it can start, which means the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returns an agent or VM identity. The failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment; no evidence of a broader platform outage or user-traffic incident is present in the supplied packet.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 147s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: near-identical Unschedulable message (146s), latencyMs=150840, no evidence keys collected
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent — consistent with the pod never starting
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=150424, check timed out waiting for pod to become schedulable before the runner gave up

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; if the pod never schedules, no VM ID or state is ever returned

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod is unscheduled

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:179-187: remote-agent-create is marked required=true with degradedAfterFailures=1, so a single failure triggers a degraded signal for the remote-agents feature
possibleCauses: Primary: The kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable resource on the 2 eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing running remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero capacity for new pods. Preemption is explicitly reported as not helpful, meaning no lower-priority victims exist to evict.

Secondary: A prior eval run or production workload created remote-agent pods that were not cleaned up, holding the kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new scheduling. The eval runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1883), but if a previous run crashed before cleanup, leaked pods could be holding capacity.

Tertiary: The 4 remaining nodes do not carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource label or do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, meaning the schedulable node pool for remote agents is structurally limited to 2 nodes and any saturation of those nodes causes a total scheduling blackout for this feature.

Lower confidence: A cluster-level change (node drain, node failure, or resource quota reduction) may have reduced the effective kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity below what is needed to run concurrent eval probes. No infrastructure change evidence is present in the supplied packet to confirm this.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pods VM Capacity Exhausted on Production Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes cannot schedule the required kata.peerpods.io/vm pod because 2 nodes report insufficient kata peer-pod VM capacity and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never schedules, the eval runner's createAgent call never returns a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is ever written and the expected-output contract is fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler cannot place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource report that resource as exhausted (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the two eligible nodes and the four mismatched nodes are structurally ineligible. The pod remains Unschedulable for ~147 seconds until the eval times out, preventing agent creation entirely. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity or configuration failure localized to the remote-agent pod scheduling path in the production Kubernetes cluster; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Swarm Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-05T11:50–11:55Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never completed, no agent was provisioned, and the expected-output contract received zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message all missing).
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm runtime in production-api has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across the two nodes that carry that resource type. The remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, so preemption is also impossible. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure that prevents any remote agent pod from being created; it is not a code defect in the eval runner or the expected-output contract. The eval failure is a direct consequence of the scheduling failure — no pod means no agent, no agent means no evidence, and no evidence means the contract validation error fires for all five required fields.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 146s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

sibling.remote-agent-create: identical Unschedulable message, latencyMs=150424, endedAt=2026-07-05T11:50:34.463Z — the earliest of the three failures, confirming the scheduling block predates the runtime check.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message, latencyMs=150575, endedAt=2026-07-05T11:53:05.038Z — sequential failure chain consistent with a persistent resource exhaustion condition.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=150840 — all three checks timed out at ~150 s, consistent with the scheduler's unschedulable wait period rather than an application-level error.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent from the evidence object, consistent with the probe never reaching the createAgent call at run-status-probes.mjs:1918.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no partial response was captured, confirming the failure occurred before any API interaction.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918; this call requires a schedulable pod and would not return if the pod is stuck unschedulable.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or a prior eval run consumed all available VM slots and they have not been released, leaving zero capacity for new remote agent pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod spec targets a node label or taint that only 2 of 6 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are also the only ones with kata.peerpods.io/vm, creating a single point of capacity failure with no fallback.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote agent pods from a previous eval run that did not clean up via withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs:1916), holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new scheduling.

Lower confidence — a cluster scaling event (node removal, node NotReady) reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes below the minimum needed to absorb concurrent eval scheduling; no node-health evidence is present in the packet to confirm or deny this.

reproductionSteps.label: Re-run only the remote-agent-runtime eval against production-api to confirm the scheduling failure is still present
reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow. Expect the same Unschedulable message if the resource exhaustion persists.

reproductionSteps.label: Run all three remote-agents checks together to confirm the shared scheduling dependency
reproductionSteps.details: All three should fail with the same Unschedulable message if the root cause is cluster-level.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and used capacity on the two eligible nodes
reproductionSteps.details: Run kubectl describe nodes against the two nodes that carry kata.peerpods.io/vm and check the Allocatable and Allocated resources sections for vm slot counts.

reproductionSteps.label: List all pods currently requesting kata.peerpods.io/vm to identify any leaked or zombie pods
reproductionSteps.details: Use kubectl get pods --all-namespaces with a field selector or label filter for the remote-agent workload to find pods that are Running or Pending and holding vm slots.

reproductionSteps.label: Check node affinity/selector on the remote agent pod spec to confirm only 2 of 6 nodes are eligible
reproductionSteps.details: Retrieve the pod spec for a remote agent workload and compare its nodeSelector or affinity rules against the labels on all 6 cluster nodes.

affectedAreas.label: Kubernetes swarm cluster — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler message directly names 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 2 nodes as the blocking condition (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

affectedAreas.label: Remote agent pod scheduling — node affinity/selector
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes and eliminating any preemption fallback (failed-check.message).

affectedAreas.label: remote-agents feature — all three checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature (features.json lines 183–185) failed with the same scheduling error, indicating the entire feature's eval surface is blocked by the infrastructure condition.
affectedAreas.details: remote-agent-create (required=true) and remote-agent-state (required=true) are required checks; their failure contributes to feature degraded/outage status per degradedAfterFailures=1.

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — remote-agent-runtime probe branch
affectedAreas.reason: The probe at lines 1913–1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote', which requires a schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm pod. The pod never schedules, so no evidence is collected and the contract validation fails.

affectedAreas.label: Expected-output contract — remote-agent-runtime
affectedAreas.reason: The contract at lines 266–270 requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message; all five are missing because the agent was never created (expected-output.missing-required-evidence).

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the two eligible nodes and compare against current pod consumption to determine whether the cluster is at a hard ceiling or whether leaked pods are holding slots.

Audit running and pending pods in the remote-agents namespace for any zombie pods from prior eval runs that did not complete the withCleanup path (run-status-probes.mjs:1916); terminate any confirmed leaks to free VM slots.

Determine whether the node affinity/selector intentionally restricts remote agent pods to only 2 of 6 nodes; if the restriction is unintentional or outdated, evaluate whether additional nodes can be labeled to expand the eligible pool.

If the cluster is at a hard capacity ceiling, engage the infrastructure team to provision additional kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (additional nodes or increased VM slot allocation on existing nodes) before the next eval run.

Note that remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true in features.json (lines 183–184); with degradedAfterFailures=1 (line 187), a single failure of either required check is sufficient to mark the remote-agents feature as degraded. Confirm the current feature health status reflects this.

After restoring scheduling capacity, re-run all three remote-agents checks and verify that the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime receives all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) and that the message assertion ('hello from aura') passes.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run remote-agent-runtime eval to confirm persistence of scheduling failure
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion is still active or has self-resolved since the 2026-07-05T11:55Z failure window.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used on all cluster nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly measures remaining VM slot capacity on each node and confirms whether exhaustion is the active blocking condition.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List all pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources to detect leaks or zombies
recommendedVerifierProbes.command: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.containers[].resources.requests["kata.peerpods.io/vm"] != null) | {name: .metadata.name, namespace: .metadata.namespace, phase: .status.phase}'
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies any leaked remote agent pods from prior eval runs that are holding VM slots and preventing new scheduling.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect node labels on all 6 nodes to verify affinity/selector coverage
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms how many nodes satisfy the remote agent pod's nodeSelector or affinity rules, validating the '4 nodes didn't match' count and identifying whether a label drift has occurred.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run all three remote-agents sibling checks together to confirm shared scheduling dependency
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: If all three fail with the same Unschedulable message, the shared-infrastructure hypothesis is confirmed. If only one fails, the cause is check-specific.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows that kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is non-zero and no pods are currently consuming it, the scheduling failure has a different cause (e.g., a node label mismatch or a Kubernetes admission webhook blocking the pod).

If re-running the eval immediately after this investigation produces a passing result with all five evidence fields present, the exhaustion was transient (e.g., a prior eval run's pods were released) rather than a persistent capacity ceiling.

If only remote-agent-runtime fails while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state pass in a subsequent run, the failure is isolated to the runtime check rather than a shared scheduling dependency, which would disprove the shared-infrastructure hypothesis.

If the node affinity/selector on the pod spec matches more than 2 of the 6 nodes, the '4 node(s) didn't match' message would need a different explanation (e.g., a recently applied taint or label change on those 4 nodes).
If a cluster autoscaler event log shows a new kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable node was added after the failure window, the exhaustion may have been a transient spike rather than a sustained ceiling.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity across all cluster nodes before attempting remote agent creation, surfacing resource exhaustion as a distinct 'warn' or 'fail' status rather than a scheduling timeout.
Add a remote-agent-pod-cleanup eval that verifies no orphaned remote agent pods are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots after each eval run cycle, catching withCleanup failures before they accumulate.

Add a node-affinity-coverage eval that asserts the number of nodes matching the remote agent pod's nodeSelector/affinity is above a minimum threshold (e.g., >= 3), alerting on label drift before it causes scheduling failures.

Consider a synthetic scheduling dry-run eval (kubectl --dry-run=server) that validates a remote agent pod spec is schedulable before the full probe attempts createAgent, enabling faster failure detection with a more actionable error message.
